title: AP-MT062-AcpTurnDiscipline

scope.summary:
GOAL: Enforce ACP sequential-turn discipline on top of the MT-061 client core so that steering a running ACP session is SAFE, HONEST, and OBSERVABLE. ACP turns are strictly sequential: the protocol has NO mid-turn steer primitive; the only mid-turn interventions are session/cancel (a notification; the agent MUST then settle the in-flight session/prompt with stop reason cancelled) followed by a new session/prompt. This MT delivers three behaviors: (1) steer requests targeting an ACP session while a turn is running are QUEUED via the MT-002 steer queue and delivered as the next session/prompt after the current turn reaches a terminal stop reason; (2) callers receive an explicit capability signal — because AdapterCapabilities.steer_mid_turn=false (MT-061), a steer submission returns a typed SteerAccepted::QueuedNextTurn outcome (never a silent inline-injection claim); (3) an explicit cancel-then-reprompt escalation path exists for callers that demand immediate steering: cancel the running turn, await the cancelled stop reason, then immediately prompt with the composed steer content.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/acp/turn_discipline.rs (queue binding, delivery loop, escalation path, typed outcomes) plus small wiring edits in acp/mod.rs and acp/client_core.rs (turn-terminal hook that triggers queue drain). Integration tests in src/backend/handshake_core/tests/acp_turn_discipline.rs against the MT-061 fixture agent (extended with a long-running scripted turn and cancel compliance).

DETAILED SPEC:
- QUEUEING: a steer request arriving while an ACP turn is in flight is enqueued on the MT-002 steer queue bound to that session (FIFO per session). The submission response is a typed outcome carrying { accepted: QueuedNextTurn, queue_position, blocking_turn_id, queued_at } — the caller always learns the steer was NOT injected mid-turn. This deliberately mirrors the governed-broker precedent (.GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge/agent.mjs busy-queue: control.busy_queued / ACCEPTED_QUEUED / queue_depth / blocking run id / FIFO drainQueuedRequestsForSession) — READ-ONLY reference; the product implementation lives on the MT-002 queue, not on JSONL files.
- DELIVERY: when the running turn settles with ANY terminal stop reason (end_turn, max_tokens, max_turn_requests, refusal, cancelled, unknown-typed), the queue drains: the head steer becomes the next session/prompt on the same ACP SessionId. Drain continues turn-by-turn (one prompt per queued steer; ACP cannot batch turns). Drain must be re-entrant-safe: a single drain driver per session (mirror the drainingSessions guard concept from the bridge), no double-prompt, no lost steer.
- CANCEL: session/cancel is sent as an ACP notification; the adapter then AWAITS the in-flight session/prompt settling with stop reason cancelled (protocol guarantee: agent MUST return cancelled). The turn terminal state is TurnCancelled; queued steers survive a cancel (they deliver on the now-idle session) unless the caller explicitly flushes the queue.
- ESCALATION (cancel-then-reprompt): a steer submitted with urgency=Immediate triggers: (a) enqueue at queue head, (b) session/cancel, (c) await cancelled settlement with a bounded deadline — if the agent does not settle within the deadline, escalate to supervisor kill via MT-005 and settle the turn as a typed failure, (d) drain delivers the steer as the next prompt. The whole escalation is a single auditable operation with a correlation id.
- OBSERVABILITY: every enqueue, dequeue/delivery, cancel request, cancelled settlement, escalation step, and queue flush emits a typed EventLedger event carrying session id, turn id, correlation id, and queue depth; the sequence is reconstructable from durable state alone (HBR-INT-007). Cross-agent steer messages carry typed routing fields per HBR-SWARM-004 (target_role, target_session, correlation_id).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the MT-002 steer queue contract/API and the MT-061 turn terminal-state hook points before writing code.
2. Implement the typed steer-submission outcome (QueuedNextTurn { queue_position, blocking_turn_id, queued_at }) returned whenever the target ACP session has a turn in flight; when idle, the steer is delivered immediately as a session/prompt and the outcome says DeliveredAsTurn.
3. Bind the MT-002 per-session FIFO queue to the ACP session; implement the single-driver drain loop triggered by the MT-061 turn-terminal hook.
4. Implement session/cancel dispatch + awaited cancelled settlement; map to TurnCancelled.
5. Implement the urgency=Immediate escalation path (queue-head insert, cancel, bounded await, MT-005 kill fallback, drain) under one correlation id.
6. Implement explicit queue flush (typed, ledgered) so a caller can abandon queued steers; flushed steers settle with a typed Flushed outcome, never vanish.
7. Emit typed EventLedger events for every transition; wire HBR-INT-009 tier evidence.
8. Extend the fixture agent with: a scripted long turn (streams updates until cancelled), correct cancel compliance (settles prompt with cancelled), and an idle mode.
9. Author the integration tests listed in expected_tests.
10. Run the proof targets; record queue/cancel timings in test output for the validator.
forbidden_paths: .GOV/** (the bridge is READ-ONLY reference for parity; never edited by this WP)
src/frontend/** (no GUI surface in this MT)
acceptance_criteria: A steer submitted while an ACP turn is running returns a typed QueuedNextTurn outcome with queue_position, blocking_turn_id, and queued_at — proven by test; no code path claims mid-turn injection for an ACP session.
A steer submitted to an idle ACP session is delivered immediately as session/prompt with a DeliveredAsTurn outcome.

When the running turn settles (each terminal stop reason covered), the queue drains FIFO: queued steers become subsequent session/prompt turns on the same ACP SessionId, one turn per steer, no loss, no duplication — proven by a test queuing >=3 steers.
Drain is re-entrant-safe: concurrent terminal events / double-trigger cannot double-prompt (single drain driver per session) — proven by a stress test.
session/cancel settles the in-flight prompt with stop reason cancelled and the turn maps to TurnCancelled; queued steers survive the cancel and deliver afterwards — proven by test.

urgency=Immediate performs cancel-then-reprompt as one correlated operation: queue-head insert, cancel, awaited cancelled settlement, steer delivered as the very next prompt — proven by test measuring the delivered order.
A fixture agent that ignores cancel past the bounded deadline triggers the MT-005 supervisor kill fallback and a typed turn failure — proven by test; no infinite wait.
Explicit queue flush settles all queued steers with a typed Flushed outcome and ledger events; nothing disappears silently.
Every enqueue/delivery/cancel/escalation/flush emits typed EventLedger events with correlation ids and queue depth; a test reconstructs the full sequence from the ledger alone (HBR-INT-007).
cargo build -p handshake_core green; all listed tests pass headless (HBR-QUIET-001).
implementation_notes: PROTOCOL FACT: ACP has no mid-turn steer; do not invent one. steer==queued-next-turn is the honest contract this MT makes explicit to every caller (orchestrator models included via MT-106 policy surface later).

Bridge precedent (READ-ONLY): .GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge/agent.mjs queueGovernedRequestOnBusy + drainQueuedRequestsForSession implement the same single-active-run + FIFO-drain + queue-depth-visible discipline against JSONL/registry state. The product version binds to the MT-002 queue and EventLedger instead; behavior parity is measured in MT-065.
The bounded cancel deadline must be configurable (env or config surface) with a conservative default; record the default in the test output. A non-compliant agent is a real July-2026 ecosystem risk.
Cancelled turns still produce partial TurnItems already streamed; those remain on the event bus/ledger — do not retract them.

Do not edit the MT-002 queue implementation; if the queue API lacks something (e.g., head-insert for escalation), implement the minimal extension in THIS MT's files only if the MT-002 surface allows composition, else record a typed dependency blocker per HBR-STOP-004.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend MT: turn discipline is a session-runtime behavior; proof is ledger/TraceProjection reconstruction per HBR-VIS-004. Steering GUI surfaces belong to other WP-017 families.

target_entries: Agent sessions: steering an ACP session — steer==queued-next-turn semantics, cancel-then-reprompt escalation, queue flush

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FLIGHT_RECORDER: steer-queued, steer-delivered, cancel-requested, cancelled-settled, escalation, and flush are business events — FR emit per MT-161 kinds when landed, else DEFERRED-with-reason.
INTERNAL_DIAGNOSTICS: expose per-session queue depth, in-flight turn age, and cancel-await state to the open diagnostic-event API — WIRED or DEFERRED-with-reason.
PALMISTRY: a cancel-await that hangs past deadline is exactly the freeze class the external watcher exists for — register the bounded-await as a tracked liveness window, or DEFERRED-with-reason.
risk_if_missed: Steering an ACP session either blocks, silently drops, or falsely claims mid-turn injection; MT-065 duty-parity (per-turn steering of repo-gov workflows) cannot be proven; orchestrator callers build on dishonest steer semantics.

risks: RISK-1: Fake steering — a code path that writes the steer into the running turn's stream (or claims injection) would fabricate a capability ACP does not have; callers would trust phantom steering.
RISK-2: Lost or duplicated steers — racy drain (multiple drivers, terminal-event double-fire) can drop a queued steer or prompt it twice; both corrupt the governed workflow.

RISK-3: Unbounded cancel wait — an agent that never settles cancelled hangs the session forever (the validator-observed hang class from WP-KERNEL-012 MT-045 validation is precedent for how expensive this is).
RISK-4: Silent queue flush — dropping queued steers without typed settlement makes work vanish unattributably.
RISK-5: Escalation ordering bug — a steer marked Immediate that lands behind older queued steers delivers stale instructions after the urgent one.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): steer_mid_turn=false is structural (MT-061); the only steer outcomes for a busy ACP session are QueuedNextTurn or the explicit escalation path; tests assert no other outcome exists.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): single drain driver per session + re-entrancy stress test + FIFO order assertion over >=3 queued steers.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): bounded cancel deadline with MT-005 supervisor kill fallback and typed failure settlement; dedicated non-compliant-agent test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): flush is an explicit typed operation; every flushed steer gets a Flushed settlement event; ledger reconstruction test covers flush.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): escalation inserts at queue head under one correlation id; ordered-delivery test asserts the urgent steer is the very next prompt.

research_provenance.source: agentclientprotocol.com (session/cancel notification semantics: agent MUST settle in-flight prompt with cancelled; strictly sequential turns; stop reasons end_turn/max_tokens/max_turn_requests/refusal/cancelled) + .GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge/agent.mjs (verified busy-queue/drain/cancel precedent: queueGovernedRequestOnBusy, drainQueuedRequestsForSession, ENQUEUE_ON_BUSY -> ACCEPTED_QUEUED with queue_depth + blocking run id, drainingSessions re-entrancy guard, timeout kill-tree settlement) + WP-017 stub risks_unknowns (ACP no-mid-turn limitation and cancel-then-reprompt mitigation).
corrections: Cancel-then-reprompt is the ONLY immediate-steer path on ACP; the contract makes it an explicit escalation with bounded deadline instead of a hidden default.
Queue authority is the MT-002 steer queue (product), not JSONL sidecar files; the bridge's file-based queue is precedent for behavior, not for storage.
